UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                        BEFORE THE
                          FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION

Northern Indiana Public Service                               )        Docket No. EL26-36-000
Company LLC                                                   )
                                                              )
v.                                                            )
                                                              )
Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc.                )


     MOTION TO INTERVENE AND COMMENTS OF THE OFFICE OF THE ILLINOIS
                          ATTORNEY GENERAL

           Pursuant to Rule 214 of the Rules of Practice and Procedure of the Federal Energy

Regulatory Commission (“Commission” or “FERC”), 18 C.F.R. § 385.214(b), the People of the

State of Illinois, by its Attorney General, Kwame Raoul (the "People" or “IL OAG”), request to

intervene in the above-captioned proceeding. Additionally, pursuant to Rule 211 of the

Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure, the IL OAG submits these comments in response

to the Complaint filed by Northern Indiana Public Service Company LLC (“NIPSCO” or

“Company”) against Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc. (“MISO”) on December 29,

2025 (the “Complaint”). The IL OAG requests that the Commission grant its motion to intervene

and accept the comments on the Complaint submitted herein.

I.         MOTION TO INTERVENE

           Illinois law provides that the Illinois Attorney General "shall have the power and duty on

behalf of the people of the State to intervene in, initiate, enforce, and defend all legal proceedings

on matters relating to the provision, marketing, and sale of electric . . . service whenever the

Attorney General determines that such action is necessary to promote or protect the rights and

interests of all Illinois citizens, classes of customers, and users of electric . . . . services.” 1 Illinois


1
    15 ILCS 205/6.5(c).

                                                     1
 law also provides that the “Attorney General shall be a party as a matter of right to all proceedings,

investigations, and related matters involving the provision of electric, natural gas, water, and

telecommunications services before the Illinois Commerce Commission, the courts, and other

public bodies." 2

        The People satisfy the requirements of Rule 214 of the Commission’s Rules of Practice

and Procedure that an intervenor have or represent “an interest which may be directly affected by

the outcome of the proceeding, including any interest as a . . . consumer.” 3 The People represent

Illinois ratepayers in MISO who may pay the charges associated with NIPSCO’s R.M. Schahfer

Generating Station Units 17 and 18 (“Impacted Schahfer Units”) spread over the MISO

north/central region. Accordingly, the People request that the Commission grant this Motion to

Intervene in this proceeding.

II.     COMMENTS

        In its Complaint, NIPSCO seeks a mechanism for the Company to obtain rate recovery

under FPA Section 202(c) for the costs of operating the Impacted Schahfer Units, which were

scheduled to retire on December 31, 2025. The units are remaining open due to the Department of

Energy’s Order on December 23, 2025. 4 NIPSCO is requesting the same recovery mechanism that

was approved by FERC for Consumers Energy Company for operation of the J.H Campbell

Generating Plant (“Campbell Plant”). 5

4

5
  Consumers Energy Co. v. Midcontinent Indep. Sys. Operator, Inc., 192 FERC ¶ 61,158 (2025) (“Consumers
Energy Order”), order on reh’g, 193 FERC ¶ 61,228 (2025) (“Consumers Energy Rehearing Order”).

                                                      2
         The IL OAG represents the People of the State of Illinois 6 and their interest in receiving

reliable electric services at the least possible cost. 7 Ratepayers in central and southern Illinois may

be subject to the costs of keeping the Impacted Schahfer Units open because they are located in

the MISO north/central region.

        Relying on the Federal Power Act Section 202(c) 8 and Section 301(b) of the Department

of Energy Organization Act 9, the Department of Energy stated that an emergency exists in the

Midwest region of the United States and ordered the Impacted Schahfer Units to remain open.10

Section 202(c), however, is subject to certain conditions where “an emergency exists by reason of

a sudden increase in the demand for electric energy, or a shortage of electric energy or of facilities

for the generation or transmission of electric energy or of fuel or water for generating

facilities…” 11 While the validity of DOE’s use of 202(c) is not at issue in this FERC case,

importantly, the DOE Order is subject to rehearing, and its legality will likely be challenged

outside of FERC.

        At issue in this proceeding are costs and cost allocation. Assuming the DOE has the legal

authority to order the Impacted Schahfer Units to remain open, which the IL OAG does not

concede, FERC should order a MISO stakeholder proceeding to ensure that ratepayers will have a

role in determining cost allocation and to ensure that costs rates are just and reasonable.




6
  Illinois ratepayers are served by two Regional Transmission Organizations, MISO and PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.
(“PJM”). Central, and Southern Illinois are encompassed by MISO Local Resource Zone 4 and a small portion of
Northwest Illinois is included in MISO Local Resource Zone 1. See MISO Tariff, Attachment VV, Map of Local
Resource          Zone          Boundaries,         https://docs.misoenergy.org/miso12-legalcontent/Attachment_VV_-
_MAP_of_Local_Resource_Zone_Boundaries.pdf. The service area of Commonwealth Edison Company, the load
serving entity for Illinois electricity customers in Northern Illinois, is encompassed by PJM’s ComEd Zone. See PJM
Open Access Transmission Tariff, Attachment J, PJM Transmission Zones, https://agreements.pjm.com/oatt/4443.

11

                                                        3
         A.       Under the assumption that the DOE Order stands, FERC should order MISO
                 to develop a stakeholder process to ensure that ratepayers subject to the Order
                 have a forum to address cost allocation and to ensure that rates are just and
                 reasonable.

        There are several states in the MISO region, and more specifically the north/central region

addressed in the Complaint, whose energy resources and prices will be affected by the DOE Order.

This includes Illinois ratepayers who are already facing high capacity charges, transmission

charges, and energy prices. The costs of running the Impacted Schahfer Units allocated throughout

MISO north/central will only add to the burden ratepayers are already facing. The overall costs are

unknown, but likely expansive, given that these units were slated to retire. There will likely be

major repair costs, including the potential costs of rebuilding Unit 18. 12

        FERC should require a MISO stakeholder process that is fair to consumers. Primarily,

FERC should order the stakeholder process to ensure that the charges associated with the plant and

cost allocation are based on the principle of cost causation where the cost causers are the cost

payers. “FERC is not authorized to approve a pricing scheme that requires a group of utilities to

pay for facilities from which its members derive no benefits, or benefits that are trivial in relation

to the costs sought to be shifted to its members.” 13 FERC must ensure that cost recovery and cost

allocation are just and reasonable, particularly when there are ratepayers who are not benefitting

from, nor causing, the costs.

        Notably, the DOE Order is only effective for 90 days, but the DOE may extend the Order

indefinitely beyond the 90 days. For example, the Campbell 202(c) Order has already been




12
   Amanda Durish Cook, Enviros Warn NIPSCO Against Rebuilding Coal Unit on DOE Emergency Order, RTO
Insider, L.L.C. (January 7, 2026), https://www.rtoinsider.com/122917-enviros-warn-nipsco-against-rebuilding-coal-
unit/ (last accessed January 20, 2026).
13
   Illinois Com. Comm'n v. FERC, 576 F.3d 470, 476 (7th Cir. 2009).

                                                        4
 extended by the DOE twice following the initial order. 14 Approving NIPSCO’s request would

constitute a piecemeal approach, given that the DOE has demonstrated that it may extend and may

institute new 202(c) orders. The MISO region could be subject to future orders, including orders

affecting plants in Illinois. 15 A stakeholder process at MISO, to address how plants such as the

Schahfer Units will be compensated, would allow stakeholders to address 202(c) orders more

efficiently than repeated filings and continuous litigation at FERC.

        Under NIPSCO’s proposed approach, costs would be spread across MISO’s north/central

region without determining the reliability benefit for those ratepayers, which is the same approach

proposed by Consumers Energy. Unlike in MISO, when this situation occurred in PJM for the

Eddystone Plant, PJM and its members initiated a Critical Issue Fast Path process, along with PJM

states and other stakeholders, to develop a cost recovery mechanism, as the PJM Tariff did not

adequately cover this issue. 16 This allowed for stakeholder feedback prior to PJM’s cost allocation

filing in which it requested approval of its cost allocation and revisions to its tariff to add a

Responsibility to Pay 202(c) Charge. 17 FERC should order a similar process for MISO prior to

approval of NIPSCO’s filing. A MISO stakeholder process will allow for state and ratepayer

engagement and transparent analysis of costs and benefits, which is necessary before costs are

imposed on ratepayers in MISO.

                                                       5
 III.   CONCLUSION

       WHEREFORE, for the foregoing reasons, the Office of the Illinois Attorney General

respectfully requests that the Commission deny the Complaint and order a stakeholder process at

MISO to address cost allocation for 202(c) orders.
